compatibility_impact: process_step_catalog S09 output_contract updated to IndicatorVector; legacy IndicatorSnapshot references resolve via alias.
decision: IndicatorVector is the canonical contract; IndicatorSnapshot is registered as an alias of it.
problem: Contract name divergence: canonical schema is IndicatorVector, but process step S09 and the manifest bundle label the same payload IndicatorSnapshot.
rationale: IndicatorVector carries a versioned JSON Schema (primary E2 artifact) and is canonical_candidate; IndicatorSnapshot is source_defined_only, appearing only as a process-step label (E3 corroboration). The evidence hierarchy ranks the schema above the label, and both names denote the same payload, so a single contract with an alias is correct.

compatibility_impact: event_models OrderIntent.side repointed to BUY/SELL enum; OrderSide(LONG/SHORT) audited for any legitimate consumer, else removed.
decision: BUY/SELL is canonical. The Pydantic OrderIntent.side must be corrected to a BUY/SELL enum (the TradingSide enum already present in the same file).
problem: OrderIntent.side vocabulary conflict: JSON schema enum [BUY,SELL] vs Pydantic OrderSide enum [LONG,SHORT].
rationale: Three independent lines agree: (1) contract-first — the versioned schema is the interface the model must conform to; (2) domain semantics — an OrderIntent is an order instruction (BUY/SELL), not a position (LONG/SHORT); (3) execution boundary — the MT4/MQL4 bridge uses OP_BUY/OP_SELL. The model's OrderSide=LONG/SHORT conflates position-side with order-side and is the defect.

compatibility_impact: New CSV contract authored with its own schema; event model reconciled to schema; producer/consumer step links updated for both.
decision: Split into two contracts. 'ReentryDecision' retains the decision-event contract (reconciled to schema ReentryDecision@1.0, which is authority over the drifted model); the CSV persistence row becomes a distinct contract with its own schema. Proposed name ReentryMatrixOutcome — FINAL NAME PENDING OWNER CONFIRMATION.
problem: Name collision: event_models.ReentryDecision (decision event) and csv_models.ReentryDecision (persisted matrix row) are divergent shapes sharing one name.
rationale: The two shapes model different entities at different boundaries (event bus vs CSV transport) and map to distinct process steps (re-entry decision vs matrix-lookup persistence); both are real and needed, so delete/merge would lose information. The versioned schema models the decision event, so it keeps the name.

compatibility_impact: Registries receive regenerated packet-derived fields only; no stale packet is ingested.
decision: Regenerate all 27 packets from current catalogs + file inventory at HEAD (POSIX path normalization, derived-complement forbidden lists) before ingestion.
options: Regenerate from current sources at HEAD then ingest
problem: 27 context packets are stale (generated 2026-05-18), use Windows backslash paths, and carry over-broad enumerated forbidden lists. Ingest as-is or regenerate?
rationale: Ingesting stale projections would inject non-normalized paths and enumerated (non-derived) forbidden lists into the authored registries — precisely the projection-to-authority contamination the SSOT design prevents. Regeneration keeps the module enrichment value while dropping the defects. Prerequisite: a working packet generator pinned to HEAD; stale packets stay quarantined until then.

compatibility_impact: Candidate implementation only; no canonical cutover in this decision.
decision: Author an explicit governed crosswalk artifact (dag_process_crosswalk) mapping DAG node id -> canonical step id, each row carrying a mapping_basis. process_step_catalog remains authority; unmapped nodes go to needs_review; DAG edges/gates/SLAs are ingested incrementally for crosswalked nodes only. Ambiguous rows are ratified by the owner.
options: Inline mapping inside the ingestion script
Exclude the DAG until a crosswalk exists
problem: DAG graph uses descriptive node ids; process_step_catalog uses canonical step ids. Where does the node->step mapping live and who owns it?
rationale: Consistent with the existing identity_crosswalk.json pattern for module aliases; keeps the mapping auditable and ratifiable rather than buried in a script, and avoids over-blocking useful DAG evidence.

compatibility_impact: Candidate implementation only; no canonical cutover in this decision.
decision: Retire 'component' as a distinct governed entity. If a component-level grouping is ever needed, derive it from module/work-cell records rather than authoring a parallel registry. Archive components/registry.yaml as out-of-domain; drop the reserved component_ids column when reusing EA-REG generator logic.
options: Stand up a distinct component registry (11th registry)
Derive components from module/work-cell records if ever needed
problem: No component authority exists in the canonical registries; only components/registry.yaml (an out-of-domain 'CLI Multi-Rapid' catalog) and a reserved component_ids column in EA-REG logic remain.
rationale: The only components artifact belongs to a different platform, and nothing in EAFIX references a component authority (component_id appears only in an unrelated UI sense). A dedicated component registry would be disproportionate; module + work-cell already provide the needed granularity.

compatibility_impact: No change to authored records; snapshot classified never-write-target.
decision: Do not promote. The generated snapshot is a parity/diff baseline only; any gap is re-authored from primary source. Verified zero delta: authored registry and snapshot cover the identical 97 contracts, so there is nothing to promote.
options: Promote snapshot records into the authored registry
Do not promote; snapshot is a diff/parity baseline only
problem: Should generated-snapshot records (contract_registry.current.json) be promoted into the authored contract_registry.jsonl?
rationale: A generated projection must never become authority (core SSOT invariant); promotion would invert the source-of-truth direction. Empirically the promotion set is also empty.
